{{Top|leg}}
'''Fan-tan''' was a [[Gambling/Legends|gambling]] game that could give players a high payoff. The game was played at the [[Fifteen Moons Casino/Legends|Fifteen Moons Casino]] on [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]]. [[G0-16]] was a fan-tan [[Dealer droid/Legends|dealer droid]] in the [[Casino/Legends|casino]].

==Description==
Fan-tan was a game of chance that involved the buying of "sticks" and wagering on the number of sticks left in a quiver hidden at the center of the fan-tan table. [[Dealer droid/Legends|Dealer droids]] were used in fan-tan, with the ones in the [[Fifteen Moons Casino/Legends|Fifteen Moons Casino]] in [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]] programmed to use facial cues to decide whether or not players wanted to place a wager. The rules stated that the droid could not backtrack to take a bet as that would be unfair to other players.<ref name="Scoundrel">''[[Scoundrel's Luck]]''</ref>

During a round of betting, players could buy sticks and place wagers. After all players had made their wagers, the dealer droid would retrieve a number of sticks and announce the number before moving onto the next round of betting. As each round of betting progressed, the payout outs decreased, such as going from five-to-one to four-to-one.<ref name="Scoundrel" />

==History==
Han Solo played a game of fan-tan at the Fifteen Moons Casino shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. The [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] was attempting to turn the credits earned for [[Rescue of Princess Leia/Legends|rescuing]] [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] into an amount large enough to pay off [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]. The other players at the table included two [[Nuiwit]]s, a [[Togorian/Legends|Togorian]], and a [[Khoan]]. During the game, the dealer droid, [[G0-16]] drew a number of sticks from the hidden quiver, announcing the total being sixteen and the  odds for the next round being five-to-one. A round of betting followed, during which the Togorian bought five sticks and wagered fifty [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] on the "one."<ref name="Scoundrel" />

With the betting round concluded, the droid retrieved twelve sticks from the quiver announcing a total of twenty-eight and the payout odds falling to four-to-one. Solo intended to double his money at four-to-one odds, preparing three hundred credits to wager. Distracted by a tug on his leg, Solo looked away from the table as G0-16 turned its attention on the smuggler. Because Solo's face was turned, the dealer droid assumed he did not want to bet and moved on. Solo objected that his bet had been missed, with the droid informing him that he could not backtrack to take a bet. A [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] [[pit-boss]] intervened and Solo's bet was allowed to be taken. Solo then had the choice of betting on the "three" or the "one."<ref name="Scoundrel" />

{{RPGseed}}
Solo chose the "three" and won the hand, gaining 5,700 credits. The dealer inquired if Solo wanted to let the bet ride, but the smuggler took his tokens as he did not let that amount of money ride.<ref name="Scoundrel" /> 
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
During the adventure, the player has the choice for Han to bet on "three" or bet on "one." The adventure states that betting on "one" is a lower payout but has more chance of being a guaranteed win, while "three" is risky with a larger payout. If the player chooses the option to bet on "one", then Han loses the hand and is reduced to only eight hundred credits for the remainder of the adventure. Because of this, the player is not allowed to take any options that involve paying more than four hundred credits in one go.<ref name="Scoundrel" />

If the player chooses the option to bet on "three", then Han wins the hand and has no money worries for the rest of the adventure and has no restrictions on how many credits can be spent at once. This article assumes that Han won the hand to ensure that the most favorable outcomes for the adventure are available.<ref name="Scoundrel" />
